subject: humanities
passage: The Book of Kells, an illuminated manuscript of the four Gospels now held at Trinity College Dublin, was made around 800 CE on roughly 340 leaves of calfskin vellum. Its pages are crowded with interlaced knots, spirals, and tiny animals, some so intricate that they can be fully appreciated only with a magnifying glass. Despite centuries of study, neither the names of the monks who produced it nor the exact place where the work was begun ______ known with certainty, though many scholars favor a monastery on the Scottish island of Iona.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: When two subjects are joined by "neither ... nor," the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Here the closer subject is "the exact place," which is singular, so the verb must be singular. The present-tense "favor" shows that the sentence describes what is known today, so "is" is correct.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Are" is plural and agrees with "names," but with "neither ... nor" the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the singular "place."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Were" is plural, but the nearer subject "place" is singular.
explanation.C: Correct. The singular verb "is" agrees with "the exact place," the subject closer to the verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Have been" is plural, but the nearer subject "place" is singular.
